channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: Macron visits Malaysia as France seeks closer defence and rare earths ties
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron will meet Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim in Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday to discuss strengthening defence, trade, energy and critical minerals co-operation. Macron's two-day visit, his first since 2017, comes ahead of the countries' 70th anniversary of diplomatic relations, with both sides seeking a strategic partnership.

item.title: Trump heads to Asia for historic nuclear talks with China and Russia
item.description: US President Donald Trump headed to Asia on Monday for economic talks and a planned trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin on nuclear issues and the war in Ukraine. Trump also raised the possibility of meeting North Korean leader Kim Jong Un during his visit.

item.title: The advice Biden got from Mitt Romney, and other takeaways from his memoir
item.description: Biden's memoir "Promise Me, America," which drops Tuesday, recounts his 2020 run for the presidency, his years in the White House and his tumultuous 2024 run.

item.title: Live: Russian attacks target bridges in Kyiv, knocking out heating and water
item.description: Russian strikes hit two major bridges in Kyiv late Monday, part of an overnight attack that damaged critical infrastructure and disrupted heating and water in parts of the capital, its mayor said. Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky had warned of an attack by Russia in the coming days even as negotiators representing Kyiv as well as Europe and the United States held talks on future negotiations with Russia aimed at finding a path to end the war.

item.title: Russian strikes hit two key bridges in Kyiv, disrupting water and power supplies
item.description: Russian forces struck two major bridges crossing the Dnipro River in Kyiv late Monday, damaging critical infrastructure and causing water and power cuts in parts of the Ukrainian capital, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said. The attacks came as Moscow launched a wider wave of drone and missile strikes across Ukraine, including in the regions of Cherkasy and Kharkiv.

item.title: WATCH: NYC teen builds candle business with refillable cement containers
item.description: What started as helping his sister make candles for a birthday party at age 13 has turned into a thriving business for New York City teen Christon Lennon.

item.title: WATCH: Meet the rental car manager going viral for keeping customers calm during ground stop
item.description: Perley Provost, manager of Enterprise Rent-A-Car at Denver International Airport, shares how he kept stranded passengers calm and hydrated during Friday's widespread ground stop.

item.title: United Airlines briefly has 'systemwide' disruption to departing flights
item.description: United said there is no indication that this was a cybersecurity-related issue.

item.title: Trump Asia trip live updates: Logistical hurdles with a Trump-Kim Jong Un meeting
item.description: Trump will participate in the first-ever trilateral meeting with Putin and Xi.

item.title: Ukraine hits key Crimea bridge with drones
item.description: "I think the Ukrainians are trying to send a message to the Russians with this - 'If you hit our bridges we can hit yours,'" reports Gulliver Cragg from Kyiv.

item.title: WATCH: Trump blames Biden administration for FAA ground stop & other stories
item.description: Nationwide FAA ground stop resulted from equipment failure, says administrator; Anthropic to price its IPO this week; NOAA reports strong El Niño expected to peak in the New Year

item.title: Chase outage disrupts online banking and Zelle payments in United States
item.description: American users of several major banking apps and online portals reported outages on Monday, according to the monitoring site Downdetector.com, with one institution ruling out a cyberattack as the cause. Among those affected by the outages were Bank of America, JPMorgan Chase and the popular money transfer app Zelle.

item.title: La Francophonie 'waning in global influence': Linguistic institutions becoming 'less important'
item.description: François Picard is pleased to welcome Phil Clark, professor of international politics at SOAS University of London. The diplomatic crisis between Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of Congo spilling out at the Francophonie summit in Phnom Penh for all to see has exposed an unexpected shift in their relations. Clark says that "nobody expected Rwanda to back down in this way" following President Macron's request that Paul Kagame withdraw Louise Mushikiwabo's candidacy for a third term.

item.title: Iran live updates: Tankers attacked in Strait of Hormuz, UKMTO says
item.description: President Donald Trump announced "major combat operations" against Iran on Feb. 28.

item.title: Europe hunts for Palantir alternatives as militaries seek to limit US dependence
item.description: As Europe's ​defence ministries look to limit dependency on American technology and major software company Palantir Technologies for critical military functions, a growing number of firms within the region are competing for their business. FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney speaks with Arthur Holland Michel, journalist and researcher specialising in emerging military technologies.

item.title: California sues OpenAI over hacking risks
item.description: The state's attorney general started investigating OpenAI after the Hugging Face attack and now says this attack was "entirely foreseeable" due to OpenAI's poor security practices.

item.title: Trump says he needs funding for air traffic control after ground stop
item.description: US ​President ​Donald Trump, pressed on a ​technology ‌failure ⁠that ‌grounded thousands of ⁠flights last week, ​on ‌Monday told reporters ‌that ​the government needed funding for upgrade ​to ​air traffic ​control equipment. FRANCE 24's Monte Francis speaks with Sheldon Jacobson, Professor of Computer Science at the University of Illinois. He explains that "the Republicans have had full control of the House and the Senate since the President came in. They controlled everything. If they needed the money and wanted the money they could have approved the money. The fact that they didn't, in the the different bills that have been passed, suggests that it's more than just money that is going on here".

item.title: Trump blames ground stop on old tech that had 'heart attack'
item.description: Friday's ground stop resulted in thousands of cancelled flights.

item.title: Rogue AI: California sues OpenAI over "Hugging Face" and other cyberattacks
item.description: The US state of California has filed a lawsuit against OpenAI over the "Hugging Face" and other cyberattacks, accusing the ChatGPT maker of knowingly testing dangerous advanced AI models without adequate safeguard. Meanwhile, the US Commerce Department has tightened rules over the export of US technology, aiming to close a loophole around remote access to advanced AI chips.

item.title: US judge strikes down Trump visa restrictions on foreign students, journalists
item.description: A US federal judge has struck down a Trump administration policy that would have sharply limited the length of time foreign students and journalists could stay in the country, ruling that the proposed restrictions were unlawful and would undermine opportunities for international education.

item.title: Rwanda to host hub for rejected EU migrants
item.description: In tonight's edition, five European countries are negotiating a deal to deport rejected asylum seekers to Rwanda. Also, the Democratic Republic of Congo and Rwanda's political animosity spills over at the Francophonie Summit in Cambodia. And in Tunisia, young women are increasingly turning towards weightlifting and bodybuilding as a form of self-expression.

item.title: November 17 blackout hoax: How a conspiracy theory went viral around the world
item.description: A conspiracy theory claiming a worldwide “blackout” will hit on November 17 has spread across social media, cutting electricity, internet and banking services. The rumour stems from a routine US FEMA emergency alert test, but was amplified by cryptocurrency accounts, misleading claims about EU preparedness advice and references to The Simpsons. Recent technology outages, flight disruptions and cyberattacks have added to public anxiety, helping turn a routine test into a global blackout hoax.

item.title: Pope concludes South America homecoming, reassures faithful after cancer scare
item.description: Pope Leo XIV finished Monday his 12-day tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru reiterating his advocacy for social justice, environmental protection and the importance of community. Just a month after undergoing lung cancer surgery, the 71-year-old pontiff drew millions of faithful across South America, where he spent nearly two decades as a missionary.

item.title: The new faces of the US Congress
item.description: The United States Congress is about to welcome dozens of new faces. A majority of them, Democratic, after the "blue wave" in the midterm elections. FRANCE 24's Washington correspondent Fraser Jackson catches up with one of these new lawmakers as they go through orientation as they prepare to take office in January. He speaks with Katy Padilla Stout, U.S. Representative-elect for Texas's 23rd congressional district.

item.title: 'Everybody's shell-shocked': GOP operatives face 2028 prospects after midterm defeats
item.description: GOP sources told ABC News the party leaned on culture wars over costs and lost key Latino voters. Some doubt JD Vance is still the presumptive 2028 nominee.

item.title: Should Ukraine trade Donbas for NATO membership?
item.description: President Volodymyr Zelensky asserting that the United States has asked him about a straight-up swap Russia gets the Donbas, the rest of Ukraine gets NATO membership, a guarantee against Moscow later having a second go and annexing the entire country. Whether or not the offer’s real, serious or that either side would accept it. We’ll ask if the talk of partition signals some kind of turning point in a nearly five-year war that's also a brutal stalemate.

item.title: Trump says he 'would not mind' if Jensen Huang is reinstated as Nvidia CEO
item.description: President Donald Trump said Monday morning that he "would not mind" if Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO of Nvidia.

item.title: EU nations unveil Rwanda deal for migrant return hub
item.description: Five EU countries including Germany and Denmark on Monday unveiled a deal to establish a migrant deportation centre in Rwanda -- the first such facility outside the bloc. The group, also comprising Austria, Greece and the Netherlands, has been gunning to open a "return-hub" despite rights groups' concerns, after the European Union cleared the way with a recent toughening of migration rules. FRANCE 24's Dave Keating reports from Brussels.

item.title: Supreme Court rebuffs Trump administration appeal over DEI funding cuts
item.description: The Supreme Court has rejected a Trump administration appeal on DEI funding cuts to academic research

item.title: UEFA backs France's Diallo to stand against Infantino in FIFA election
item.description: European football's governing body UEFA has given its "unanimous" backing to French Football Federation chief Philippe Diallo to stand against incumbent Gianni Infantino in March's FIFA presidential election, it said in a statement Monday. Under its Slovenian president Aleksander Ceferin, UEFA has led the opposition to Infantino since his announcement in late July of a project to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors. FRANCE 24's Selina Sykes speaks with Dr. Emanuel Macedo de Medeiros, Co-founder and Global CEO of the Sport Integrity Global Alliance.

item.title: 'A futuristic debate now very real': Why the world is struggling to regulate killer robots
item.description: Representatives from 128 nations are meeting in Geneva on Monday to decide whether to move ahead with negotiating legally binding rules around the use of AI-powered weapons that can kill without human involvement. FRANCE 24 spoke with artificial intelligence researcher Vincent Boulanin to find out just what is at stake.

item.title: U.S. tightens controls on remote access to AI technology amid Nvidia fallout
item.description: The new rule closes a loophole that existed that allowed Chinese companies to still access advanced AI chips remotely, despite U.S. restrictions on their physical sale to China.

item.title: Czech mass protests: Media is the first casualty 'when you want to attack democracy'
item.description: As hundreds of thousands of people gather in Prague to protest the Czech government's proposal to replace public broadcasting licence fees with direct state funding, Delano D'Souza is pleased to welcome Bára Stárek, Executive Director of Díky, že můžem. Stárek warns that the proposed changes offer "no real safeguards" against political influence, pointing to developments in Slovakia and Hungary. She also drew a parallel with the Velvet Revolution of 1989, recalling that "we didn't have a free media and we only had a state media" under communist rule. "Media is the first (line of) attack when you want to attack democracy," she said. With the legislation expected to reach Parliament in January, Stárek believes the demonstrations will continue if the government refuses to engage in any discussions.

item.title: U.N. talks seek to rein in 'killer robots' as fears over AI weapons grow
item.description: Countries are meeting in Geneva to negotiate rules on weapons that can select and kill targets without human intervention. But with the U.S., Russia and Israel resisting legally binding controls, campaigners fear the window to act is closing.

item.description: Judge William Sullivan scheduled a hearing on Monday morning to formally schedule a trial date in the case.

item.title: Robert Pattinson: British actor will be the next James Bond
item.description: British actor Robert Pattinson is set to become the next James Bond in the long-running 007 spy franchise. Discussions over the casting of the new James Bond had been going on for months, with Pattinson emerging as one of the frontrunners from the outset.

item.title: Russia's war on Ukraine: 'Americans want to have a deal whatever the cost for both Ukraine & Europe'
item.description: Delano D'Souza is pleased to welcome Grégoire Roos, Director of the Europe and Russia and Eurasia Programmes at Chatham House. As European countries prepare to take part in the next round of Ukraine peace talks, Roos questions whether having five European representatives could weaken their negotiating position. "The other option is to realize that it dilutes the negotiating power of Europe. And I would lean towards that," he says, proposing Finnish President Alexander Stubb as a possible representative. Roos also points to differences between Washington and European governments over negotiations with Russia. While "the Americans do absolutely want to have a deal whatever the cost for both Ukraine and Europe," he argues that European governments have little choice but to maintain pressure on Moscow, which has yet to abandon its "maximalist demands."

item.description: British actor ​Robert Pattinson will be the next James Bond, Amazon MGM Studios announced on Monday, ​taking on the role after Daniel Craig's departure from the long-running spy series.

item.description: Lindsay Clancy is due to face a retrial next March over the killing of her three young children.

item.description: Authorities say a 500-foot Atlantic asphalt tanker collided into the American Heritage cruise ship on Friday, causing the ship to fall on its side and capsize in just 22 minutes.

item.description: Helen Haines, the Australian politician who lost both legs after an alleged attack, has said she is "full of gratitude" upon leaving hospital.

item.description: This global campaign brings public awareness and attention to Sanfilippo Syndrome, a rare, terminal genetic disorder that causes dementia in children for which there is currently no cure.

item.title: WATCH: Heartwarming update on Punch the Monkey
item.description: The baby macaque at Japan’s Ichikawa City Zoo became a viral sensation after turning to an IKEA toy for comfort. Nine months later, Punch has joined the troop and taken an interest in a baby macaque.
